doc.title: Eddie Metz Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, October 3, 2015

title: Advice: listen and support
summary: Advice for young musicians: wear a tee shirt, listen with a mental mixing board, and play a supporting role.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Advice to young musicians starting out

blocks.x: And you actually answered the question, I didn’t even get to — I was going to say do you have any advice for up and coming musicians?

And listen. Listen to everybody that’s around you. Take that little mixing board in your head. If you look at a mixing board and you know what it’s like. There’s usually a solo button or a mute button for each channel. So think of each instrument as having its own little channel. You want to hear more trumpet? Press that solo button in your head and the trumpet comes right to you. You want to hear more bass? Hit that. So that’s how I try to explain it to kids, about listening. The listening was so ingrained into me, about listening to what’s going on. Because drums are a support instrument. We get our chance to play our solos but we’re in a support role. Drums and bass. We’re supporting everybody else. And our job is to make them sound as good as possible. Because I don’t want to be standing out there playing a horn. I like to hide in my cage behind the drums you know. Standing out front, I’ve gotten better about it, about playing solos and stuff, but I’d rather try and make somebody sound good in a support role, that’s part of a team effort. If you think of it as a sports team, everybody knows their role, and you just go out and play your role and keep your ears open and to be able to respond instantly to anything that might come up, rhythmically, harmonically, whatever it is, change of style, change of feel. I like to pride myself — I can play just about any style that’s thrown my way from rock to funk
to R&B to Latin to Gospel, to whatever. So I immerse myself into the music. I’d love to have a Steely Dan gig. Please.
Me too. You like all the same stuff I do.
